Technology Stack and Architecture (V2 Apple Frosted Glass & 5-Preset Architecture):
- Approved Core Stack:
  - Frontend: React (^19)
  - Language: TypeScript (^7) with strict typing (avoid `any`)
  - Build Tool: Vite (^8)
  - Dev Server: Runs deterministically on port 3000 (http://localhost:3000)
  - Styling: Vanilla CSS / modern CSS custom properties (variables.css, components.css, globals.css)
  - Package Management: npm
  - Deployment: Vercel static hosting
- 5-Preset Color Theme Architecture:
  - State Management: ThemeContext.tsx providing ThemeId = 'royal' | 'cyber' | 'mocha' | 'emerald' | 'carbon'.
  - DOM Synchronization: document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', theme) and <meta name="theme-color"> updates.
  - Local Persistence: localStorage key 'portfolio-color-theme' (defaults to 'royal').
  - CSS Custom Properties: Dynamic tokens in variables.css for each [data-theme] preset (--color-base, --color-secondary, --color-accent, --glass-bg, --veil-bg, --glass-border, --glass-shadow, --color-btn-glow, etc.). Zero hardcoded colors in components.css and globals.css.
- Fluid Motion & 3D Stack:
  - Global Smooth Scroll: Lenis (^1.3) with SmoothScrollProvider in src/components/motion/SmoothScroll.tsx synchronized with GSAP ticker; mobile touch preservation; data-lenis-prevent modal wheel support.
  - Scroll Animation: GSAP (^3.15) + ScrollTrigger for viewport card scale-ups and parallax.
  - Micro-Interactions: Framer Motion (^14.6) for hero staggered float-up entrances and magnetic hover tracking (src/components/motion/Magnetic.tsx).
  - Persistent 3D WebGL Layer: Three.js (^0.186), @react-three/fiber (^9.8), and @react-three/drei (^10.7) in HeroScene.tsx, mounted at root in App.tsx with fixed viewport positioning, scroll/mouse reaction, and dynamic useTheme() color reactivity.
- Apple-Style Frosted Glass Architecture:
  - Global Frosted Veil: .global-glass-veil at z-index 0 with var(--veil-bg) and var(--glass-blur).
  - Floating Glass Panels: Navigation, Cards, Experience entries, Skill groups, and Modal use var(--glass-blur), var(--glass-border), and var(--glass-shadow-hover).
  - Section Transparency: All section containers maintain transparent backgrounds.
- Architectural Model:
  - Primarily static frontend application with data-driven TypeScript modules under src/data/.
  - Local React state only; no global state libraries (Redux, Zustand) allowed.
  - Verification Requirement: Every change must be verified with `npm run build` (tsc && vite build).

Pre-Stage 6 Hotfix — Education Section Theme Contrast Verified:
- Visual Defect Reproduced & Diagnosed:
  In dark mode ([data-theme="dark"]), the Education section displayed a theme contrast bug where:
  1. Card 1 (MANIT Bhopal, priority 'high'): Rendered with a pure white background and blue outline, causing near-white text on white background (1.05:1 contrast).
  2. Card 2 (DU, priority 'medium'): Rendered with a dark slate background (#1e293b) and crisp light text (13.35:1 contrast).
  3. Cards 3 & 4 (Class XII and X, priority 'low'): Rendered with near-white backgrounds (#fafafa) and light gray borders, causing severe text washout against light foreground text.
- Confirmed Root Cause:
  In src/styles/components.css:
  - `.education-entry.priority-high` had hardcoded `background: var(--color-white);` (#ffffff) and `border-color: var(--color-accent);` (#3b82f6).
  - `.education-entry.priority-low` had hardcoded `border-color: var(--color-gray-200);` (#e7e7e7) and `background: var(--color-gray-50);` (#fafafa).
  - Neither used theme-aware semantic tokens.
  - In contrast, `.education-entry.priority-medium` had no background override, naturally inheriting `.education-entry`'s semantic `background: var(--color-surface);` (#1e293b in dark mode), which explained why only Card 2 rendered correctly.
  - Additionally, `.entry-location` used `color: var(--color-text-muted);` (#64748b), which provided only 3.07:1 contrast against the dark card surface (#1e293b), falling below WCAG AA 4.5:1 requirement.
- Fix Applied:
  In src/styles/components.css:
  1. Removed `background: var(--color-white);` from `.education-entry.priority-high` so all cards inherit semantic `background: var(--color-surface);` (#1e293b in dark, #ffffff in light).
  2. Preserved `.education-entry.priority-high { border-color: var(--color-accent); }` and added `:hover { border-color: var(--color-accent-hover); }` to gracefully highlight the current Master's program across themes.
  3. Removed `background: var(--color-gray-50);` and `border-color: var(--color-gray-200);` from `.education-entry.priority-low`, replacing with semantic `border-color: var(--color-border);`. Retained existing lower-priority font scale distinction (.entry-degree font-size: base).
  4. Added `:hover` (`border-color: var(--color-border-strong);`) and accessible `:focus-visible` ring (`outline: var(--focus-ring-width) solid var(--focus-ring-color); outline-offset: var(--focus-ring-offset);`) to `.education-entry`.
  5. Added explicit `color: var(--color-text-primary);` to `.entry-degree` for defensive styling.
  6. Replaced `color: var(--color-text-muted);` on `.entry-location` with `color: var(--color-text-secondary);`, raising location text contrast from 3.07:1 to 5.71:1 in dark mode (exceeding WCAG AA 4.5:1) while maintaining 7.81:1 in light mode.

[RECALL System Architecture & Layering Overview]
RECALL is a persistent memory engine designed for AI coding agents with dual client surfaces:
1. Agent Surface: Stdio JSON-RPC MCP server (`recall_mcp/server.py`) exposing 9 FastMCP tools for coding agent integration.
2. Human Surface: Web Dashboard (`frontend/`) built with React 19 (v19.3.0), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, and Vite, consuming HTTP JSON REST endpoints (`api/`).

Architecture Layers:
- Client Adapters: `recall_mcp/` (FastMCP stdio) and `api/` (FastAPI HTTP REST).
- Application Core (`recall_core/`): Central orchestration facade (`MemoryManager`), `ContextAssemblyService`, `CustomInstructionService`, and bootstrap composition root (`bootstrap.py`). Backward-compatibility shims maintained in `core/recall_core/`.
- Domain Contracts (`contracts/`): Pure dataclasses and typed schemas (`Memory`, `Project`, `Session`, `CustomInstruction`, `RetrievalRequest`, `ConflictResolutionResult`, `Result[T]`).
- Persistence Layer (`database/`): SQLite connection manager with WAL mode (`database/connection.py`), `SQLiteUnitOfWork`, typed repositories, schema DDL (`database/schema/ddl.py`), and versioned migrations (`database/migrations/`).
- Semantic Retrieval & Intelligence (`intelligence/`): Vector indexing via ChromaDB (`database/repositories/semantic_index_repo.py`), local SentenceTransformer embeddings (`intelligence/embeddings.py`), lexical/semantic retrieval (`intelligence/retrieval.py`), and rule/LLM conflict arbitration (`intelligence/conflict.py`).

Canonical vs. Derived State:
- Implemented Canonical Truth: SQLite (`~/.recall/recall.sqlite3`) is the sole canonical source of truth for all projects, sessions, memories, lineage graphs, and custom instructions.
- Derived Semantic State: ChromaDB (`~/.recall/chroma/`) is derived vector state storing embeddings exclusively for memories with `status='active'`.
- Index Rebuildability: Active memories can be rebuilt from SQLite canonical storage at any time via `MemoryManager.rebuild_semantic_index()`. Historical (superseded/archived) memories and custom instructions are not vector-indexed in ChromaDB.
- Encapsulation: All client surfaces communicate strictly with the core facade (`MemoryManager`) and never touch repositories or databases directly.

[RECALL Data and Execution Flows]
End-to-end request pipelines across client surfaces and storage:

1. Memory Capture Flow:
- Ingestion: MCP client calls `recall_save_memory` or Web Dashboard sends `POST /memories`.
- Validation: Request payload validated against typed domain contract `MemoryCreateRequest` (content presence, scope, optional project_id / session_id).
- Orchestration: `MemoryManager.create_memory()` executes.
- Canonical Storage: `SQLiteMemoryRepository.create()` within `SQLiteUnitOfWork` writes row to SQLite `memories` table with UUID, timestamps, status='active', and metadata.
- Semantic Store: If canonical write succeeds, `ChromaSemanticIndexRepository.index_memory()` embeds memory content via `SentenceTransformerEmbeddingService` and upserts into ChromaDB collection. If `supersedes_id` is specified, the superseded record is removed from the vector index.
- Failure Isolation: If vector indexing encounters an error, canonical SQLite persistence is preserved and an indexing warning is returned in result metadata.

2. Context Assembly & Retrieval Flows:
- Context Assembly Flow: Agent calls `recall_get_context` via MCP stdio. `MemoryManager.assemble_context()` delegates to `ContextAssemblyService.assemble()`, which loads scoped active project memories and global active memories from SQLite, loads superseded memories if `include_historical=True`, loads active custom instructions, and performs vector/keyword retrieval if a query is provided.
- Context Query Flow: Web Dashboard sends `POST /context/query` to search memories. This endpoint directly calls `MemoryManager.retrieve()` for semantic and keyword matching, returning supporting memory hits rather than full assembled context.
- Authority Handling in Retrieval: `ContextAssemblyService` provides active memories and custom instructions side-by-side in `AssembledContext`. It does not filter or prune conflicting memories during assembly.

3. Compaction Flow:
- Trigger: Agent runs `recall_compact` or dashboard calls `POST /context/compact` with `project_id` and `max_active_memories`.
- Identification: Active memories retrieved and sorted chronologically by `updated_at`.
- Consolidation: Oldest N active memories exceeding cap are selected and combined into a single new summary memory with provenance='compaction_summary'.
- Lineage Tracking: `SQLiteMemoryRepository.create_lineage()` records parent-child relationships (`parent_id=source_id, child_id=summary_id, relationship='supersedes'`).
- Archival & Vector Deletion: Source memories updated to `status='superseded'`. When status changes from active, `ChromaSemanticIndexRepository` removes them from the vector collection. Deep historical superseded memories beyond 100 are transitioned to `status='archived'`.

4. Conflict Detection & Arbitration Flow:
- Trigger: Initiated via `MemoryManager.detect_and_resolve_conflicts()` or `POST /conflicts`.
- Deterministic Evaluation: `DefaultConflictResolver.apply_deterministic_rules()` evaluates candidates against active custom instructions and provenance ranking (`explicit_user_update` > `user_explicit` > `inferred`), active status, and recency.
- Model Arbitration: If deterministic rules leave residual ambiguity, `DefaultConflictResolver` delegates to local LLM adapter (`OllamaConflictAdapter`) with cloud fallback on context window overflow.
- Non-Hallucination Policy: If ambiguity persists without high confidence, RECALL outputs status='unresolved' or 'abstained' rather than fabricating certainty.

[RECALL Architectural Constraints & System Invariants]
Fundamental design constraints enforced across the codebase:

1. Canonical Truth & Derived Index Invariant:
- SQLite (`~/.recall/recall.sqlite3`) is the sole canonical source of truth for all entities: projects, sessions, memories, lineage graphs, and custom instructions.
- ChromaDB (`~/.recall/chroma/`) is derived semantic state storing vectors exclusively for `status='active'` memories. It is NOT authoritative.
- Rebuildability: Active memories can be rebuilt from SQLite at any time via `MemoryManager.rebuild_semantic_index()`. Historical (superseded/archived) memories and custom instructions are not vector-indexed in ChromaDB.
- Known Limitation: SQLite schema defines `memory_index_metadata` and `instruction_index_metadata` tables, but they are unpopulated in the current implementation.

2. Client Encapsulation Boundary:
- Client surfaces (`recall_mcp/` and `api/`) must strictly interact with the core domain facade `MemoryManager`.
- External modules must never access private attributes such as `_uow` or directly query repositories. AST regression tests (`test_api_package_has_zero_uow_access` and `test_api_module_has_zero_uow_access`) enforce this rule continuously.

3. Instruction Precedence & Authority Enforcement:
- Authority Hierarchy: Explicit user custom instruction > Explicit user update / supersession > Current valid canonical memory > Older historical memory > Local 1B-3B model arbitration > Unresolved / abstain.
- Enforcement Boundary: This hierarchy is strictly enforced inside `DefaultConflictResolver.apply_deterministic_rules()` during conflict resolution. In standard context assembly, active memories and custom instructions are provided side-by-side to the agent without destructive filtering.
- LLM Arbitration Limit: The conflict resolution LLM is strictly an arbiter of residual ambiguity; it cannot override explicit user instructions, mutate canonical storage, or fabricate certainty.

4. Relational & Schema Constraints:
- Scope rules: SQLite CHECK constraint `((scope = 'global' AND project_id IS NULL) OR (scope = 'project' AND project_id IS NOT NULL))` enforces that project memories/instructions MUST specify a `project_id`, and global items MUST have `project_id = NULL`.
- Foreign keys: Enabled via PRAGMA `foreign_keys = ON` in all connection contexts. Cascading deletions clean up sessions, memories, and lineage.

5. Concurrency & Multi-Process Model:
- Independent processes: The MCP stdio server and HTTP API run as separate OS processes, each initializing its own SQLite connection via `DatabaseConnection`.
- In-Process Concurrency: Thread safety within each process is managed by `ThreadSafeConnection` via `threading.RLock()`. RECALL does not use a connection pool.
- SQLite Multi-Process Mode: SQLite WAL mode allows concurrent readers alongside a single writer. Connection configuration sets `timeout=30.0s` and PRAGMA `busy_timeout=5000ms`.
- ChromaDB Limitation: ChromaDB's in-memory index cache is local to each process. Mutations made in one process are not pushed to other running processes until re-query or client reload occurs. Centralized multi-process deployments require an external vector service or dedicated indexing worker.

6. Non-Hallucination Policy:
- When conflict resolution cannot resolve contradictory context deterministically or statistically, RECALL reports `unresolved` or `abstained` rather than fabricating artificial certainty.
